title: Make your phone battery last
summary: When you don't know when you will be able to recharge.
steps: Turn on the strongest battery-saving mode.
Switch to airplane mode when you are not expecting a call; turn it off briefly at set times.
Turn brightness down to the minimum, switch off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, location and mobile data.
Close apps and avoid video, games and the phone's flashlight.
Keep the phone warm (in an inside pocket): cold drains the battery.
tips: A weak signal uses much more power: in an area with no coverage, airplane mode is essential.

title: Recharging without a power socket
summary: Power bank, car, solar, hand crank.
steps: Power bank: keep it permanently charged in your kit.
Car: cigarette-lighter socket with a USB adapter, engine running, outdoors only (never in a closed garage).
USB solar panel: point it at full sun, charge a power bank first rather than the phone directly.
Hand-crank radio or torch with a USB port: a few minutes of charging for an emergency call.
warnings: Running an engine in an enclosed space = deadly risk of carbon monoxide.

title: Lighting during a power cut
steps: Headlamp: keeps your hands free, ideal for cooking or giving first aid.
Battery or rechargeable LED lamps: low consumption, no fire risk.
Tip: put a headlamp under a bottle of water to light a whole room.
Candles: only under supervision, on a stable holder, away from curtains and children.
warnings: Candles are a frequent cause of fires during power cuts.

title: Using a car battery safely
summary: A 12 V energy reserve to light and recharge.
steps: Connect a 12 V to USB converter, or a cigarette-lighter socket with clamps.
Red on the + terminal, black on the − terminal, clamps tight.
Small devices only: phones, LED lamps, radio.
Don't drain the battery completely if you plan to start the car again: stop before the headlights dim.
warnings: Never connect the two terminals directly (short circuit, burns, explosion).
No flame or spark near a charging battery (hydrogen gas).

title: Sizing a small solar kit
summary: Choose a panel and a battery to recharge phones and lamps.
steps: Estimate your needs: a phone ≈ 15 Wh per charge, an LED lamp ≈ 3 to 5 Wh per evening, a radio ≈ 2 Wh.
Power bank: 20,000 mAh ≈ 70 Wh, about 4 phone charges.
20 to 30 W folding panel: about 50 to 100 Wh per sunny day (much less when overcast).
Charge the power bank with the panel during the day, then the devices in the evening.
